title: Scalar extension realizes finite completion modules
statement: Let X be a scheme, A a commutative Noetherian ring, I an ideal, C its adic completion and H the inverse limit of the constant quotient ring sheaves on X. Suppose phi: constant(C) -> H has evaluations as all its finite projections. Then scalar extension of constant finite C-modules along phi is exact on finite modules, is adic lisse of finite type, and has projection-linear isomorphisms with the completed constant quotient-module sheaves, natural in all C-linear maps. In the interfaces of [def-weil-pbc-completed-constant-realization-data], this is a module-realization record d with d.scalar = phi. There is no derived-complex conclusion here.

proof.text: Let C be the completion and J = IC. The kernel of eval_n is J^n, by the adic evaluation kernel formula and scalar restriction. The quotient first isomorphism theorem gives C/J^n = A/I^n. Its evaluation normalization proves the successor-transition square, so constant sheafification produces an isomorphism of the quotient-ring towers. Transporting the scalar phi through the induced limit isomorphism gives the canonical coefficient map for (C,J). Completion is Noetherian, so the existing flat completed-algebra theorem applies to this presentation. It proves ordinary scalar extension along phi exact; compose with exact constant-module sheafification and then the exact inclusion of finite modules. Additivity is the composite of the existing additive constant functor and additive scalar extension.

A finite C-module N is J-complete by the finite-module completeness theorem, since C is Noetherian and J-complete. Scalar restriction gives I-completeness. The map A -> C/J is surjective: lift eval_1(c) to an element a of A, and eval_1(c - a) = 0 gives c - a in J. Thus C/J is finite over A. The finite C-module N/JN is finite over C/J and hence over A. Transport this property through the canonical scalar-restriction quotient isomorphism to N/IN.

Use the finite-module tensor-to-limit comparison for the family of realization isomorphisms, its projection linearity and its naturality. To prove local lissity, choose the maximal covering sieve of the terminal pro-etale object. On every member use the same underlying A-module N. Its completeness and finite first quotient were just proved. Forget each comparison to additive sheaves and restrict it to the over-site. Its scalar condition is the supplied projection-linearity condition evaluated at the underlying over-site object. These constructions fill all fields of CompletedConstantModuleRealization with scalar phi; the scalar equality is reflexivity.

proof_origin.place: Tags 093J--093M: T4 formal quotient-tower transport proves exactness; finite complete module algebra and restriction of the comparison prove the adic-lisse local models. The tensor-to-limit comparison is isolated in the new strictly smaller lemma.

theorem completed_constant_module_model (X : Scheme.{u})
    {A : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A)
    (φ : adicLisseConstantRing X (AdicCompletion I A) ⟶ adicLisseCompletedRing X I)
    (hφ : ∀ n : ℕ, φ ≫ limit.π (adicLisseRingSystem X I) (op n) =
      (constantSheaf (ProEt.topology X) CommRingCat.{u + 1}).map
        (CommRingCat.ofHom (AdicCompletion.evalₐ I (n + 1)).toRingHom)) :
    ∃ d : CompletedConstantModuleRealization X I, d.scalar = φ
